We already have marketing support, an internal development team, established manufacturer relationships, and leadership that is invested in making marketing a stronger part of the business.

Role & Responsibilities

Marketing strategy and planning

Work with leadership to set marketing priorities, including the markets we focus on, manufacturer lines we promote, how we position ourselves, and where we spend our time and budget. Then turn those priorities into action.

Trade shows and events

Manage industry shows, customer training events, and vendor events from start to finish, including booth logistics, pre-show outreach, lead capture, staffing, follow-up, and measuring results.

Manufacturer and vendor marketing

Work with our manufacturer partners on co-op marketing funds, joint campaigns, product launches, line cards, and literature. Make sure we're representing their brands well and taking advantage of the resources they provide.

Demand generation

Manage paid media, SEO, email campaigns, content, landing pages, and list building. Track performance and understand what these efforts are producing.

Sales enablement

Create and manage line cards, spec sheets, case studies, presentations, and other materials our sales teams use in the field. The goal is simple: give our salespeople tools that are useful and that they actually want to use.

Swag, literature, and fulfillment

Manage Rust and vendor swag, printed literature, and line cards. Forecast what our sales teams and branches will need, coordinate orders, work with vendors, and keep materials organized and available.

Brand and content

Maintain a consistent voice and look across everything we put out, including customer stories, LinkedIn, newsletters, website content, and PR where it makes sense.

Measuring results

Track things like pipeline contribution, cost per lead, cost per quote, campaign performance, and where our marketing dollars are going.

What makes this role different

Manufacturer partnerships are a big part of the job

We're a partner-led business, so working with our manufacturer partners is an important part of marketing here. That includes brand standards, co-op dollars, product launches, joint campaigns, and other marketing programs.

Experience on the manufacturer or distributor side is a plus, but it's not required.

Qualifications & Profile

We're flexible on how you got here. Any of these could be a good fit:

- Marketing management at an industrial distributor, manufacturer's representative, manufacturer, or another technical industry
- A strong marketing specialist or manager at a larger industrial company who's ready for more responsibility
- Agency experience serving industrial clients, if you're ready to come in-house and work more directly with the business and its results

Deep trade show and event experience is a real plus. So is experience working with manufacturer partners and joint marketing programs.

A relevant degree, equivalent experience, or a track record that speaks for itself can all work here. We care more about what you've built and how you work than exactly where you learned it.

You like people.

This job puts you in front of customers, manufacturer partners, and our own team constantly. Trade show floors, booth duty, dinners, meetings, and plenty of conversations. It isn't a desk job with a campaign calendar.

You finish things.

There are a lot of moving pieces in marketing. You need to be organized, keep things moving, close loops, and follow through.

You take responsibility.

You'll have support and a solid foundation to work from, but you'll be responsible for keeping your areas moving and making sure things get done.

You bring ideas and can execute them.

We want someone who will look at what we're doing and find ways to make it better. At the same time, you'll need to be comfortable taking an established program and executing it well without feeling like everything needs to be redesigned first.

You're comfortable with technical people.

You don't need an engineering degree. You do need to be curious about what a flow meter or control panel actually does and comfortable sitting down with an engineer and asking questions.

You're honest about the numbers.

If a campaign didn't work, tell us. We'd rather learn from it than find a way to make the numbers look better.

- Identify opportunities for additional automations and lifecycle marketing initiatives.

- Monitor flow performance and make data-driven recommendations for ongoing optimization.

- Build recurring and ad hoc email marketing reports.

- Translate performance data into clear insights and actionable recommendations.

- Identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement across email programs.

- Communicate results and recommendations to internal teams and clients as needed.

- Comfortable interpreting email performance data and turning insights into recommendations.

Marketing Operations Specialist

Remote

Apply here

Talkdesk competes in a market where the quality of execution separates companies that grow efficiently from those that spend more to get the same result. Marketing Operations is where that execution lives. This role exists to ensure that every dollar of marketing spend, every campaign, every event, and every account-based program translates into pipeline with zero friction. That requires a system built for precision where the right prospect reaches the right person at the right time, consistently and by design.

You sit inside the Marketing team, with close partnerships across Sales and RevOps. The marketers running campaigns, events, and account-based programs are your primary stakeholders. When the system works, their work converts.

In practice, that means owning the full operational surface of marketing technology: administering and continuously improving the tools that make up our GTM stack, building and maintaining the integrations that keep data moving cleanly between systems, designing the orchestrations that automate account and contact engagement, ensuring the enrichment and data integrity standards that make every downstream decision reliable. This is an interdependent system, and this person keeps it running as a coherent, high-performing whole.

What You'll Own

- Account-Based Marketing Orchestration: Serve as the technical owner of our ABM orchestration layer. Translate signals from our intent platform into automated, sequenced actions across our marketing automation platform and CRM, working closely with campaign and field marketing teams to ensure the right programs reach the right accounts at the right moment. Getting this infrastructure right is one of the highest-impact contributions this role makes to the business.

- Marketing Technology Foundation: Own the day-to-day health of our martech systems and the workflows, API calls, integrations, and syncs that connect them to keep prospect data moving accurately through the funnel. When something breaks or underperforms, you diagnose it, fix it, and document the resolution so it does not recur.

- Agentic AI Workflow Engineering: Design and build automated workflows that use AI capabilities to evaluate qualitative signals, such as demo request notes, intent activity, and unstructured form inputs, alongside firmographic data to produce dynamic lead scores and routing decisions. You write the API calls, design the orchestration logic, test against edge cases, and iterate based on conversion outcomes. Experience shipping something to production is the bar.

- Enrichment and Insights: Build and manage the workflows that construct a complete, account-level intelligence profile from the moment a prospect engages. That means aggregating first-party behavioral signals, third-party intent data, firmographic context, and web research into a unified view that captures not just the individual contact but the broader buying committee: who across the account is engaging, with what content, and what their activity suggests about organizational priorities and pain points. That intelligence surfaces in the systems where sales and marketing work, so every follow-up is informed, relevant, and timed to the account's buying journey.

- System Documentation and Enablement: Every workflow you build or modify gets documented: field mapping dictionaries, AI orchestration logic, routing rule change logs. Beyond documentation, you actively invest in making the marketing team more self-sufficient, building self-service reporting and dashboards that allow marketers to check campaign performance, list quality, or lead status independently, and creating resources that allow colleagues to troubleshoot routine tasks and leverage AI tools without filing a request. An empowered marketing team operates with greater speed and confidence, and this role contributes meaningfully to that outcome.

Who You Are

You operate with a high degree of autonomy. You are embedded in the relevant standups, attentive to system performance, and typically ahead of issues before they surface as escalations. Your manager will set context and priorities; the execution is yours to own.

You are invested in the success of the Marketing team. You understand that the campaigns, events, and programs your colleagues execute are only as effective as the systems that support them. Leads from a field event that go unrouted, an ABM sequence that executes against incomplete data, or a high-intent inbound request that experiences significant delay before reaching an SDR all represent measurable pipeline impact. You approach your work with that accountability in mind.

You are technically strong and collaborative by nature. Marketers, Sales and RevOps are close partners. You understand their workflows well enough to anticipate where system gaps will affect their work, and communicate clearly when something is broken, when it is fixed, and why. Strong cross-functional relationships are central to this role.

You see the work through to completion. You build, test, document, and close the loop. When something you own regresses, you identify it first.

What We're Looking For

_Required_

- 3 to 5 years in B2B SaaS Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations, or a systems-adjacent role
- Hands-on marketing automation and CRM administration, including configuring and maintaining MAP-to-CRM syncs
- Demonstrated ability to build and deploy an automated workflow that calls external APIs, whether webhooks, REST APIs, or LLM endpoints, in a production environment
- Native fluency in B2B funnel mechanics: MQL definitions, lifecycle stage transitions, opportunity lifecycles, and attribution models
- Experience coaching or enabling non-technical stakeholders on new tools, AI workflows, or self-service reporting

_Strong Signal_

- Hands-on administrative experience with intent data platforms, routing engines, and ABM orchestration
- Prior experience building LLM-powered workflows for lead scoring, routing, or qualification
- Comfort reading and writing JSON, working with REST APIs, and debugging integration errors independently

How We'll Measure Success

The through-line across all of it is pipeline efficiency: more of the right prospects converting into pipeline from the programs already running, with less manual intervention and less fallout.

_30 days:_ Full audit of marketing automation-to-CRM field mapping is complete, ownership of inbound routing rules is established, and current ABM workflow patterns are mapped to identify key automation opportunities.

_60 days:_ First agentic AI workflow is deployed to staging or production. At least one major ABM orchestration sequence that previously required manual steps is automated. An initial self-service enablement resource or dashboard is delivered to the marketing team.

_90 days and beyond:_ Lead sync exception rate is at target with a monitoring process that catches regressions before Sales does. ABM orchestration operates as a reliable service layer that campaign and field marketers can brief and trust to execute. Marketing colleagues actively leverage self-service tools and AI workflows independently.

Application Question

_Required with your resume (200 words max):_

A high-intent prospect submits a demo request but never reaches the assigned SDR in the CRM. Walk us through your exact diagnostic process: which logs you check first, how you trace the break across the marketing automation-to-CRM sync and inbound routing rules, how you validate the fix, and how you would design an agentic step to evaluate the prospect's form submission notes for priority routing.
